ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: After the bloody Kalinga War, Ashoka renounced conquest by force, and royal patronage helped spread Buddhism across the subcontinent and beyond.
Inscribed on rocks and pillars, the edicts proclaimed dhamma and welfare measures, even naming Hellenistic kings as recipients of Ashoka's missions.
The agreement of 313 between Constantine and Licinius that set a persecuted sect on the road to becoming Rome's dominant institution.
King Ezana's adoption of Christianity in the fourth century made the church a major pillar of Aksumite government.
The first caliphs, successors to the Prophet Muhammad, turned a religious community into an empire reaching Syria, Egypt and Iraq.
On Christmas Day 800 Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne in Rome, sealing the alliance between the papacy and the Frankish monarchy.
Centuries of holy war in the name of faith, including the irony of 1204, when crusaders sacked Christian Constantinople.
Ismail I proclaimed Twelver Shia Islam the state religion in 1501, forging an Iranian identity distinct from his Sunni Ottoman and Uzbek neighbours.
Akbar's Sulh-i-kul, or 'peace with all', and his abolition of the jizya in 1564 contrast with Aurangzeb's return to orthodoxy.
